# Associations with fire (Q3)

<!-- readme-only -->

**What and why.** Within the Holocene lake-periods, does a period with more climate change, or
more fire, end with a larger lag, and with better or worse pace and direction? Each response is
modelled on the park, the climate change rate and fire activity together. The lake-periods of
one lake come from the same core and catchment, so their errors can be related. An AR(1) term
within each lake carries that, counted in climate periods: two lake-periods one period apart are
correlated by φ, two periods apart by φ², also where the period between them has no lake-period. Ends that rest on
a single sample are noisier, so each row is weighted by the sampling variance of its two ends,
and the parks keep different residual spread. In the Anthropocene the same responses are
compared between burned and unburned plots, in a model with the park and fire (burned or not).
Only NOCA plots burned between the two surveys, so the fire comparison is a NOCA comparison.

**How it is calculated.**

```{r step5-code}
code_snippet('R/pipeline/15_predictor_models.R', 'holocene-explanatory-model')
code_snippet('R/pipeline/15_predictor_models.R', 'anthropocene-explanatory-model')
```

**Result.**

<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r step5-results}
coefficients = read_output('community_predictor_models/model_coefficients.csv')
performance = read_output('community_predictor_models/model_performance.csv')
label = c(lag_rate = 'Lag rate', pace_effect = 'Pace contribution', direction_effect = 'Direction contribution',
  lag = 'Lag (not divided by time)', pace_effect_total = 'Pace contribution (not divided by time)',
  direction_effect_total = 'Direction contribution (not divided by time)')
coefficients |> left_join(performance |> select(metric = response, era, n, R2), by = c('metric', 'era')) |>
  transmute(Quantity = label[metric], Era = era, Term = term, Estimate = estimate, SE = std_error, df,
    t = estimate / std_error, `95% CI` = sprintf('%.3f to %.3f', conf_low, conf_high), p = p_value, n, `R²` = R2) |>
  show_table('step5_explanatory_models', caption = paste('**Table S21. Associations with fire: coefficients of the models.** Holocene:',
    'models of the lake-periods with park, climate change rate (or climate change, for the quantities not divided by time), and',
    'fire activity as fixed effects, a first-order autoregressive correlation within each lake, and weights for the number of',
    'samples at t1 and t2. Anthropocene: models of the plot pairs with park and fire (burned or unburned) as fixed effects (see',
    'Methods of the main text). Terms: siteNOCA, difference between NOCA and MORA; burnedBurned, difference between burned and',
    'unburned plot pairs. Estimates are in CCA distance (per century for the rates) for one unit of the term. SE, standard error.',
    'Two-sided t-tests on the residual degrees of freedom (df) of the model, with 95% confidence intervals (CI). n, number of',
    'lake-periods or plot pairs. R² is descriptive. The fit of the models is given in Table S22.'))
slope = function(m, t) coefficients |> filter(metric == m, era == 'Holocene', term == t)
f = function(x) sprintf('%+.2f (%.2f to %.2f)', x$estimate, x$conf_low, x$conf_high)
```

```{r step5-slope-words}
# The direction of each slope in words, from its interval, so that the text follows the fit.
say = function(m, t, what) {
  x = slope(m, t)
  if (x$conf_low > 0) sprintf('went with a larger %s (%s)', what, f(x))
  else if (x$conf_high < 0) sprintf('went with a smaller %s (%s)', what, f(x))
  else sprintf('did not go with the %s (%s)', what, f(x))
}
hol_slopes = coefficients |> filter(era == 'Holocene', term %in% c('climate_rate', 'climate_change', 'fire_activity'))
```

<!-- readme-only -->

In the Holocene, faster climate change `r say('lag_rate', 'climate_rate', 'lag rate')` and
`r say('pace_effect', 'climate_rate', 'pace contribution')`. More frequent fire
`r say('lag_rate', 'fire_activity', 'lag rate')` and `r say('direction_effect', 'fire_activity', 'direction contribution')`.
The slopes are in CCA distance per century for one more standardized unit of climate change per century,
or for one more event per century per core. `r u = read_output('cca_tracking_lake_periods.csv'); mr = range(u$fire_activity[u$site == 'MORA']); nr = range(u$fire_activity[u$site == 'NOCA']); ov = sum((u$site == 'MORA' & u$fire_activity >= nr[1]) | (u$site == 'NOCA' & u$fire_activity <= mr[2])); if (ov) sprintf('The fire values of the two parks overlap in %d of the %d lake-periods.', ov, nrow(u)) else 'The fire values of the two parks do not overlap.'` The site term
absorbs the difference between the parks, so the fire slope comes from the variation within each park
(`r paste(sprintf('%s %.2f to %.2f', c('MORA', 'NOCA'), tapply(u$fire_activity, u$site, min), tapply(u$fire_activity, u$site, max)), collapse = ', ')`
events per century per core).

The same models on the responses not divided by time (Fig. S18) use the climate change between the two ends in
place of its rate, and the slopes are in CCA distance per standardized unit of climate change or per
event per century per core. More climate change `r say('lag', 'climate_change', 'lag')`,
`r say('pace_effect_total', 'climate_change', 'pace contribution')` and
`r say('direction_effect_total', 'climate_change', 'direction contribution')`. More fire
`r say('lag', 'fire_activity', 'lag')`, `r say('pace_effect_total', 'fire_activity', 'pace contribution')` and
`r say('direction_effect_total', 'fire_activity', 'direction contribution')`. Of the
`r nrow(hol_slopes)` Holocene climate and fire slopes, `r n_away = sum(hol_slopes$conf_low > 0 | hol_slopes$conf_high < 0); n_away`
`r if (n_away == 1) 'has' else 'have'` an interval that excludes zero. They rest on `r nrow(u)` lake-periods
(`r sum(u$direction_defined)` for the pace and direction contributions). `r sf = here::here('output_paleoclimate_sensitivity', 'comparison', 'explanatory_slopes.csv'); if (file.exists(sf)) { sl = readr::read_csv(sf, show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(term != 'siteNOCA'); sm = sl[sl$conf_low_two_step > 0 | sl$conf_high_two_step < 0, ]; k = sum(sign(sm$estimate_raw) == sign(sm$estimate_two_step)); if (nrow(sm) == 1) paste0('Without the correction of the Holocene climate, the one slope whose interval excludes zero ', if (k == 1) 'keeps its sign (Appendix S4).' else 'changes its sign (Appendix S4), so it is fragile.') else sprintf('Without the correction of the Holocene climate, %d of these %d slopes keep their sign (Appendix S4)%s', k, nrow(sm), if (k < nrow(sm)) ', so they are fragile.' else '.') } else ''`
`r ab = coefficients |> filter(era == 'Anthropocene', term == 'burnedBurned') |> mutate(what = tolower(label[metric]))
ab_txt = function(d) paste(sprintf('the %s (%+.2f, %.2f to %.2f)', d$what, d$estimate, d$conf_low, d$conf_high), collapse = ', ')
lo = ab |> filter(conf_high < 0); hi = ab |> filter(conf_low > 0); no = ab |> filter(conf_low <= 0, conf_high >= 0)
paste0('In the Anthropocene (burned minus unburned plots), ', paste(c(if (nrow(lo)) paste0('burned plots had lower values for ', ab_txt(lo)),
  if (nrow(hi)) paste0('burned plots had higher values for ', ab_txt(hi)),
  if (nrow(no)) paste0('burned and unburned plots did not differ in ', ab_txt(no))), collapse = '. In addition, '), '.')`
Fire activity stays a frequency in both forms, because a count of events would grow with the length
of the lake-period.

```{r fig-6-main}

perf6 = read_output('community_predictor_models/model_performance.csv')
R2 = function(r, e) sprintf('%.2f', perf6$R2[perf6$response == r & perf6$era == e])
```

# Species contributions (Q4)

<!-- readme-only -->

**What and why.** The observed movement of a community between t1 and t2 is the sum of one
vector per species: the change in the species' share times the species' fixed position in the
CCA plane (asserted). Projecting each species' vector on the direction in which the
climate-predicted position moved says how far that species carried the community along with the
climate. This is `contrib_climate`, per century of the interval between the two vegetation samples.
A positive value means the species moved the community in the climate-predicted direction, a
negative value that it moved it against that direction. Where the observed or the climate-predicted
position did not move, the direction is undefined, and so is the contribution, so those
lake-periods and plot pairs are left out.

**How it is calculated.**

```{r step6-code}
code_snippet('R/helpers/cca_transition_contributions.R', 'contrib-climate')
code_snippet('R/pipeline/16_contributions.R', 'species-means')
```

**Result.**

<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r step6-results}
species_means = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_means.csv')
# Only the species contribution in the climate-predicted direction is shown (Bills, 24 Nov 2026).
# contrib_lag is still computed in R/pipeline/16_contributions.R.
species_means = species_means |> filter(measure == 'contrib_climate')
species_means |> mutate(value = ifelse(interval_defined, sprintf('%+.3f (%.3f to %.3f)', estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
    ifelse(present, sprintf('%+.3f', estimate), 'absent'))) |>
  select(species, site, period_type, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period_type, values_from = value) |>
  rename(Species = species, Park = site) |>
  show_table('step6_species_means', caption = paste('**Table S23. Species contributions in the climate-predicted direction per century.**',
    'Mean and 95% confidence interval (t-interval) in CCA distance per century, for each species, park, and period type: how far the',
    'species moved the community in the climate-predicted direction (positive values) or against it (negative values). "absent": the',
    'species was not found in that park and period type. Lake-periods and plot pairs in which the observed or the climate-predicted',
    'position did not move are left out.'))
```

<!-- readme-only -->

The species vectors add up to the observed movement for every lake-period and plot pair (asserted).
```{r step6-numbers}
hol = species_means |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene')
hol_away = hol |> filter(interval_defined, conf_low > 0 | conf_high < 0)
ant = species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene', interval_defined)
along = ant |> filter(conf_low > 0); against = ant |> filter(conf_high < 0)
sp_list = function(d) if (nrow(d)) paste(sprintf('*%s* (%+.3f)', d$species, d$estimate), collapse = ', ') else 'none'
park_words = function(p) { a = along[along$site == p, ]; b = against[against$site == p, ]
  part = function(d, where) if (nrow(d)) sprintf('%d moved the communities %s (%s)', nrow(d), where, sp_list(d)) else
    sprintf('none moved the communities %s', where)
  sprintf('At %s, among the species whose interval excludes zero, %s, and %s.', p,
    part(a, 'in the climate-predicted direction'), part(b, 'against that direction')) }
n_units = species_means |> distinct(site, period_type, n)
```

In the Holocene every species mean is close to zero in both parks (largest absolute value
`r sprintf('%.3f', max(abs(hol$estimate)))` CCA distance per century).
`r if (nrow(hol_away)) paste0(nrow(hol_away), ' of ', sum(hol$interval_defined), ' Holocene intervals ', if (nrow(hol_away) == 1) 'excludes' else 'exclude', ' zero (',
paste(sprintf('%s, %s, %s', hol_away$species, hol_away$site, hol_away$period_type), collapse = '; '), ').') else
paste0('None of the ', sum(hol$interval_defined), ' Holocene intervals excludes zero.')` Each Holocene mean rests on
`r paste(sort(unique(n_units$n[n_units$period_type != 'Anthropocene'])), collapse = ' or ')` lake-periods. In the Anthropocene, a
species' interval excludes zero more often. `r park_words('MORA')` `r park_words('NOCA')` Values are in CCA distance per century.

```{r step6-contrasts}
sc = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_contrasts.csv') |> filter(measure == 'contrib_climate')
sc_sig = sc |> filter(p_adjusted < .05)
```

The period types of a species are compared with Welch tests, three contrasts per species and park,
and the p-values are Holm-adjusted within each park across all species and contrasts. Of `r sum(!is.na(sc$p_value))` testable contrasts, `r sum(sc$p_value < .05, na.rm = TRUE)` have
p < 0.05 before the adjustment `r if (nrow(sc_sig)) paste0('and ', nrow(sc_sig), ' after it (', paste(sprintf('*%s* at %s, %s', sc_sig$species, sc_sig$site, sc_sig$contrast), collapse = '; '), ').') else 'and none after it.'`
`r if (nrow(sc_sig) && all(startsWith(sc_sig$contrast, 'Anthropocene'))) 'All of them set the Anthropocene against a Holocene period type.' else ''`

```{r fig-8-main}
show_figure('report/figures/main/fig_species_contributions.pdf')
```

**Fig. 7. Species contributions in the climate-predicted direction in the Holocene and the Anthropocene.** Each
species' vector is its change in share between the first and the last sampled century of a lake-period, or
between the legacy survey and the resurvey of a plot, times its fixed position in the CCA plane. The vectors
are projected on the direction in which the climate-predicted position moved. Labels at the top of each panel
give the meaning of each side of zero: a species moved the community against or following the climate-predicted
direction. Lake-periods and plot pairs whose observed or climate-predicted position did not move are left out.
Values are per century of the interval between the two vegetation samples.
Species are ordered by the maximum elevation of the plots where they occur (the 605 plot pairs, both surveys, both parks), the highest at the top. Their names are shaded by that maximum in four grey steps, lightest below 1,500 m and black above 1,900 m (key below the figure). Names in bold are species absent from the Holocene record of both parks.
Symbols are means: squares, Holocene stability periods, diamonds, Holocene climate-change periods,
circles, Anthropocene plot pairs (burned and unburned together), each with its 95% t-interval. Means whose
interval excludes zero are large and dark, and means whose interval includes zero are small and faded, with
faded intervals. A species with no
Holocene symbols in a park is absent from that park's Holocene record.
Each park has its own x scale, symmetric around zero. `r both_spans` Contributions are in CCA distance per century.

<!-- /readme-only -->

**Species contributions not divided by time.** Per century, the species contributions of the Holocene are
small partly because the lake-periods are long, and those of the Anthropocene are large partly because the
time between the two surveys is short. To test whether this explains the difference between the two eras,
we also calculated the species contributions without dividing by time (Fig. S19, Table S24).

```{r step6-totals}
st = read_output('species_contribution_models/species_means_total.csv')
# Means whose 95% interval excludes zero, for species present in that park and period type.
away = function(d) d |> filter(present, interval_defined, conf_low > 0 | conf_high < 0)
key = function(d) sort(paste(d$measure, d$species, d$site))
st = st |> filter(measure == 'contrib_climate')
hol_t = st |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene', present)
hol_r = species_means |> filter(period_type != 'Anthropocene', present)
size_t = st |> filter(present) |> mutate(era = ifelse(period_type == 'Anthropocene', 'A', 'H')) |>
  group_by(site, era) |> summarise(m = mean(abs(estimate)), .groups = 'drop')
sz = function(p, e) size_t$m[size_t$site == p & size_t$era == e]
ant_t = away(st |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene'))
ant_r = away(species_means |> filter(period_type == 'Anthropocene'))
show_figure('report/figures/supplementary/figS19_species_contributions_total.pdf')
```

Not divided by time, the mean contributions of the Holocene were `r if (all(c(sz('MORA', 'H') >= sz('MORA', 'A'), sz('NOCA', 'H') >= sz('NOCA', 'A')))) 'at least as large as' else 'not everywhere as large as'` those of the
Anthropocene (mean absolute value `r sprintf('%.3f', sz('MORA', 'H'))` against `r sprintf('%.3f', sz('MORA', 'A'))` at MORA and
`r sprintf('%.3f', sz('NOCA', 'H'))` against `r sprintf('%.3f', sz('NOCA', 'A'))` at NOCA, CCA distance). However, they varied so much among the few lake-periods that the confidence interval excluded zero for
`r nrow(away(hol_t))` of the `r sum(hol_t$interval_defined)` Holocene means (`r nrow(away(hol_r))` per
century). In the Anthropocene, it excluded zero for `r nrow(ant_t)` means, against `r nrow(ant_r)` per
century, `r if (identical(key(ant_t), key(ant_r))) 'for the same species in the same parks' else 'not all for the same species'`.
`r if (nrow(away(hol_t)) == 0 && sz('MORA', 'H') >= sz('MORA', 'A') && sz('NOCA', 'H') >= sz('NOCA', 'A')) 'Thus, within a lake-period, the species of the Holocene moved the communities in or against the climate-predicted direction at least as far as those of the Anthropocene, but too variably among lake-periods to identify which species did so.' else ''`

**Fig. S19. Species contributions in the climate-predicted direction not divided by time.** As Fig. 7 of the
main text, with the contribution of each species between t1 and t2 and not per century: how far each species
moved the community in the climate-predicted direction (positive values) or against it (negative values).
Means with 95% confidence intervals (t-intervals). Symbols, order of the species, and shading as in Fig. 7.
`r both_spans` Contributions are in CCA distance.

```{r step6-totals-table}
st |> mutate(value = ifelse(interval_defined, sprintf('%+.3f (%.3f to %.3f)', estimate, conf_low, conf_high),
    ifelse(present, sprintf('%+.3f', estimate), 'absent'))) |>
  select(species, site, period_type, value) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = period_type, values_from = value) |>
  rename(Species = species, Park = site) |>
  show_table('step6_species_means_total', caption = paste('**Table S24. Species contributions in the climate-predicted direction not',
    'divided by time.** Mean and 95% confidence interval (t-interval) in CCA distance, for each species, park, and period type.',
    'Columns as in Table S23.'))
```

# Appendix S4. Sensitivity of the results to the correction of the Holocene climate

```{r appendix-s4-setup}
s4_dir = here::here('output_paleoclimate_sensitivity', 'comparison')
s4_has = file.exists(file.path(s4_dir, 'explanatory_slopes.csv'))
s4_term_label = c(siteNOCA = 'Park (NOCA against MORA)', climate_rate = 'Climate change rate',
  climate_change = 'Climate change', fire_activity = 'Fire activity')
s4_run = c(two_step = 'two-step (main)', one_step = 'one-step', raw = 'raw')
s4_p = function(p) ifelse(p < .001, '< 0.001', sprintf('%.3f', p))
s4_read = function(f) readr::read_csv(file.path(s4_dir, f), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

The bias correction of the Holocene climate assumes that the difference between the climate products was
constant through the Holocene (Appendix S2). To assess how much the results depend on this correction, we
repeated the analysis with two other versions of the Holocene climate: with the one-step correction (step 2
alone, i.e., CHELSAcruts to CHELSA V2.1), and without correction. Among the three analyses, only the
climate-predicted positions of the Holocene communities and the climate periods can change, whereas the
observed positions, community turnover, and all quantities of the Anthropocene do not. We compared three
results among the analyses: the lag and the pace and direction contributions of each lake-period (Fig. S20,
Table S20), the differences between period types (Table S16, Fig. S21), and the associations with climate
change and fire in the Holocene (Fig. S22).<!-- readme-only --> [`R/sensitivity_paleoclimate.R`](R/sensitivity_paleoclimate.R) reruns stages 08 to 16 twice into
`output_paleoclimate_sensitivity/` and leaves the main outputs untouched. The raw TraCE21k was the
paleoclimate of the analysis until 11 November 2026. The counts below are read from the tables that the
script writes to `output_paleoclimate_sensitivity/comparison/`.<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r appendix-s4-figure}
if (s4_has) {
  s4_match = s4_read('lake_period_matching.csv')
  # Whether the three runs drew the same climate periods (same names, types and ends).
  s4_periods = s4_read('climate_periods.csv') |> select(run, period, period_type, older_cal_bp, younger_cal_bp)
  s4_catalog = split(select(s4_periods, -run), s4_periods$run)
  s4_same_periods = all(vapply(s4_catalog, \(x) isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(x), as.data.frame(s4_catalog$two_step),
    check.attributes = FALSE)), logical(1)))
  s4_lp = s4_read('lake_period_responses.csv')
  s4_kept = function(r, p, other) { x = s4_lp |> filter(response == r, site == p, is.finite(two_step), is.finite(.data[[other]]))
    sprintf('%d of %d', sum(sign(x$two_step) == sign(x[[other]])), nrow(x)) }
  s4_change = function(run) { x = s4_lp |> filter(response == 'climate_change', raw > 0)
    sprintf('%.0f%%', 100 * median(abs(x[[run]] / x$raw - 1))) }
  s4_r = s4_read('lake_period_correlations.csv')
  s4_r1 = function(resp, park, run) sprintf('%.2f', s4_r$r[s4_r$response == resp & s4_r$site == park & s4_r$run == run])
  s4_tracking = c('lag', 'lag_rate', 'pace_effect_total', 'pace_effect', 'direction_effect_total', 'direction_effect')
  s4_rr = function(park, run) { x = s4_r |> filter(site == park, run == .env$run, response %in% s4_tracking)
    sprintf('%.2f to %.2f', min(x$r), max(x$r)) }
  s4_ec = s4_read('era_contrasts.csv')
  s4_sig = function(run) sum(s4_ec[[paste0('p_adjusted_', run)]] < .05)
  s4_ec_changed = s4_ec |> filter((p_adjusted_two_step < .05) != (p_adjusted_one_step < .05) |
    (p_adjusted_two_step < .05) != (p_adjusted_raw < .05))
  # The climate and fire terms only, as in the text of Q3 (the park term is left out).
  s4_sl = s4_read('explanatory_slopes.csv') |> filter(term != 'siteNOCA')
  s4_away = function(run) sum(s4_sl[[paste0('conf_low_', run)]] > 0 | s4_sl[[paste0('conf_high_', run)]] < 0)
  s4_sl_main = s4_sl |> filter(conf_low_two_step > 0 | conf_high_two_step < 0)
  show_figure('report/figures/supplementary/figS20_paleoclimate_lake_periods.pdf', width = '75%')
} else cat('Run Rscript R/sensitivity_paleoclimate.R to fill this appendix.\n')
```

**Fig. S20. Holocene lake-periods with and without correction of the Holocene climate.** Each point is one
lake-period that the three analyses have in common, with its value without correction (x-axis) against its
value with the two-step correction of the main analysis (red) and with the one-step correction (grey), each
with its least-squares line: (A) climate change and (B) its rate, (C) the lag and (D) its rate, (E) the pace
contribution and (F) its rate, (G) the direction contribution and (H) its rate. Left: quantities between t1 and t2. Right:
their rates per century. Circles are MORA and squares NOCA. On the dashed line, a correction changes
nothing, and in the shaded quadrants, the value changes sign. The numbers in each panel are the Pearson
correlations (r), across the lake-periods of each park, between each corrected analysis and the analysis
without correction. Lake-periods in which the observed or the climate-predicted position did not move have
no pace or direction contribution. Community turnover is the same in the three analyses and is not shown. Climate
change is in SD of the legacy plots, and the other quantities are in CCA distance (left) or in CCA distance
per century (right).<!-- readme-only --> Script:
[`R/figures/supp_paleoclimate_sensitivity.R`](R/figures/supp_paleoclimate_sensitivity.R).<!-- /readme-only -->


**Fig. S21. Differences between period types with the three versions of the Holocene climate.** The
differences between the estimated means of two period types within each park (Table S16 for the main
analysis), each with its 95% confidence interval (not adjusted): filled points and solid lines with the
two-step correction of the main analysis, open circles and dashed lines with the one-step correction, and
open squares and dotted lines without correction. Upper row of each panel: MORA (blue). Lower row: NOCA
(dark red). (A) Climate change, lag, pace contribution, and direction contribution between t1 and t2. (B) Their rates per
century. Community turnover is the same in the three analyses and is not shown. Climate change is in SD of
the legacy plots, and the other quantities are in CCA distance (A) or in CCA distance per century (B). The
dashed vertical line marks zero.<!-- readme-only --> Script:
[`R/figures/supp_paleoclimate_sensitivity.R`](R/figures/supp_paleoclimate_sensitivity.R).<!-- /readme-only -->

```{r appendix-s4-text, results = 'asis'}
if (s4_has) {
  s4_lst = function(d, f) if (nrow(d)) paste(f(d), collapse = '; ') else 'none'
  # Same sign as in the main analysis (two-step correction), for the differences and the Holocene coefficients.
  s4_same = function(d, run) sign(d[[paste0('estimate_', run)]]) == sign(d$estimate_two_step)
  # Turnover is the same in the three analyses, so its differences cannot change and are left out.
  s4_era = s4_ec |> filter(startsWith(contrast, 'Anthropocene'), !response %in% c('turnover_rate', 'displacement'))
  s4_hol = s4_ec |> filter(!startsWith(contrast, 'Anthropocene'))
  s4_era_main = s4_era |> filter(p_adjusted_two_step < .05)
  s4_hol_main = s4_hol |> filter(p_adjusted_two_step < .05)
  # Significant with the same sign in another analysis.
  s4_robust = function(d, run) sum(s4_same(d, run) & d[[paste0('p_adjusted_', run)]] < .05)
  s4_era_flip = s4_era_main[!s4_same(s4_era_main, 'one_step') | !s4_same(s4_era_main, 'raw'), ]
  s4_against = c('Anthropocene - Holocene-C' = 'Anthropocene against Holocene climate-change periods',
    'Anthropocene - Holocene-S' = 'Anthropocene against Holocene stability periods')
  s4_sl_same = function(run) sum(s4_same(s4_sl_main, run))
  s4_sl_also = function(run) sum(s4_same(s4_sl_main, run) &
    (s4_sl_main[[paste0('conf_low_', run)]] > 0 | s4_sl_main[[paste0('conf_high_', run)]] < 0))
  cat(paste0('**Lake-periods.** ',
    if (s4_same_periods && all(s4_match$lake_periods == s4_match$shared_by_all[1]))
      sprintf('The three analyses had the same %d climate periods and the same %d lake-periods. ',
        nrow(s4_catalog$two_step), s4_match$shared_by_all[1]) else
      sprintf('The three analyses had %d lake-periods in common. ', s4_match$shared_by_all[1]),
    'With the one-step correction, the lag had the same sign as in the main analysis in ', s4_kept('lag', 'MORA', 'one_step'),
    ' lake-periods at MORA and in ', s4_kept('lag', 'NOCA', 'one_step'), ' at NOCA. Without correction, it had the same sign in ',
    s4_kept('lag', 'MORA', 'raw'), ' lake-periods at MORA and in ', s4_kept('lag', 'NOCA', 'raw'),
    ' at NOCA (Fig. S20C). The pace and direction contributions are given in Table S20.\n\n',
    '**Differences between the Anthropocene and the Holocene.** Of the ', nrow(s4_era_main), ' differences that were significant ',
    'in the main analysis (Table S16, Fig. S21; turnover, which the correction does not touch, left out), ', s4_robust(s4_era_main, 'one_step'),
    ' were also significant, with the same sign, with the one-step correction, and ', s4_robust(s4_era_main, 'raw'),
    ' without correction. ',
    if (nrow(s4_era_flip)) paste0('The sign changed for: ', s4_lst(s4_era_flip, function(d) sprintf('%s at %s, %s',
      tolower(response_label[d$response]), d$site, s4_against[d$contrast])), '.\n\n') else 'None of them changed sign.\n\n',
    '**Differences within the Holocene.** Of the ', nrow(s4_hol_main), ' differences between the climate-change and the ',
    'stability periods that were significant in the main analysis (', s4_lst(s4_hol_main, function(d) sprintf('%s at %s',
      tolower(response_label[d$response]), d$site)), '), ', s4_robust(s4_hol_main, 'one_step'),
    ' were also significant, with the same sign, with the one-step correction, and ', s4_robust(s4_hol_main, 'raw'),
    ' without correction.\n\n',
    '**Associations with climate change and fire in the Holocene.** Of the climate and fire coefficients whose confidence ',
    'interval excluded zero in the main analysis (', nrow(s4_sl_main), '), ', s4_sl_same('one_step'), ' had the same sign with the one-step correction (',
    s4_sl_also('one_step'), ' of them with a confidence interval that still excluded zero), and ', s4_sl_same('raw'), ' without correction (',
    s4_sl_also('raw'), ' of them with an interval that still excluded zero; Fig. S22).\n\n',
    '**Consequences for the conclusions.** ',
    if (nrow(s4_era_flip) == 0) paste0('The comparison between the Anthropocene and the Holocene does not depend on the correction ',
      'of the Holocene climate: all differences that were significant in the main analysis had the same sign in the three ',
      'analyses. ') else paste0('The comparison between the Anthropocene and the Holocene depends in part on the correction of the ',
      'Holocene climate: ', nrow(s4_era_flip), ' of the differences that were significant in the main analysis changed sign. '),
    'The results that rest on the Holocene alone depend on it more, i.e., the lags of single lake-periods, the differences ',
    'between the climate-change and the stability periods, and the associations with climate change and fire. We therefore ',
    'interpret these three results with caution.\n'))
}
```
